title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — Rom. 5:14; your form of the Apostle’s argument is not his
pass_a_gloss: Placeus turns to Rom. 5:14 (death reigned even over those who did not sin after Adam’s likeness; Adam a type of the Coming One). Garissoles rightly notices cause-from-effect—all sinned because death reigned over all—but the syllogism he frames is his own, not the Apostle’s mind.
pass_b_english: Let us come to verse 14: But death reigned even over those who did not sin after the likeness of Adam’s transgression, who is a type of the one to come.
Here you rightly observe that the Apostle infers a cause from an effect, and proves that all have sinned because death reigned over all;
and so you form the Apostle’s argument—you ought to have said, your own.
For it is far from the Apostle’s mind.
source_text: Veniamus ad vers. 14. Sed regnavit mors etiam in eos qui non peccaverunt ad similitudinem transgressionis Adae, qui est typus futuri. Hic tu recte observas Apostolum causam inferre ex effectu, ac probare, omnes peccasse, quia mors regnavit in omnes; ac sic formas argumentum Apostoli, debuisti dicere, tuum. Apostoli enim longe abest a mente.
